key_insight: For Helmholtz problems with uniaxial perfectly matched layers (UPML), optimal high-wavenumber inf-sup scaling μ ∼ k⁻¹ enables preasymptotic error estimates for linear CIP-FEM.
engineering_relevance: These results support reliable finite-element simulation of high-frequency waves in unbounded domains approximated by absorbing layers.
method: Establish wavenumber-explicit stability for full-space UPML in two and three dimensions.
Extend optimal inf-sup estimates to truncated UPML domains.
Derive preasymptotic error estimates for linear continuous interior penalty FEM.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions and demonstrate CIP-FEM effectiveness at high wavenumbers; the abstract provides no quantitative benchmark results.
watch_item: The stability theory requires sufficiently large wavenumbers and specified regularity, piecewise-power structure, and low-absorption derivative bounds for the absorption profile.
paper_title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
